summary: D1 puts each project's ready tooling in one hand-authored manifest, .concord/tooling.v1.json, whose intent fields (id, purpose, invocation, tier, notes) have no upstream source to drift from; D2 proves every derived claim at check time through scripts/check-project-tooling.py wired into check-json.py, where config_path must resolve, ci_reference must appear in a workflow file, in_ci false forbids ci_reference, and a missing manifest is a finding rather than a vacuous pass; D3 holds the CD-0043 D1 boundary by carrying facts about tools (what exists, how it is invoked) and never methodology (when an agent should choose it); D4 performs file reads only so CD-0040 D6's probe-family limit holds and executing repo-named binaries stays unopened; D5 keeps CI as one derived attribute rather than the authority, because CI enumerates only the always-on subset and the infrequent tools are the operator's stated case.
title: A project declares its ready tooling as a validated manifest
